scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-REQUESTER-FRAMING.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August; build an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and fix wrong bills.

H-AMI-READ-ISSUE.statement: AMI read errors or missing reads since August caused estimation substitutions and incorrect bills, driving dispute volume.

H-FIELD-READ-ISSUE.statement: Problems in the contracted manual meter‑read process (staffing, route execution, or delayed uploads) produced missing or erroneous reads since August, leading to billing errors and disputes.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change in billing import validation rules (DA‑RULES) since August introduced incorrect bill calculations, increasing disputes.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Dispute ticket volume rose from ~600 in June/July to 1180 in August and 1260 in September, showing a clear surge starting in August.
The billing system tariff change log contains no records, indicating that no tariff changes have been logged in the system.

The observation shows that among disputed bills, 1240 have estimated reads and 1785 have actual reads, indicating that a substantial portion of disputes arise from bills based on actual meter reads, not solely from estimation substitutions.
The route completion rate for August‑September 2026 is 0.88, below the target of 0.95, indicating that field manual read collection fell short of expected coverage during the dispute surge period.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder states that no tariff changes have occurred this year, indicating tariff changes are not a contributing factor to the dispute surge.

The observation shows that dispute tickets are being answered within the SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days against a 3‑day SLA), indicating that response speed is not the primary driver of the dispute surge.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Staff shortage of three readers since July causes delayed meter routes, leading to estimated bills for affected customers.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract confirms that route priority changes can be requested by the utility but must be executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation, reinforcing the existing authorization constraint on route updates.
